learning_objective: 🎯 Explore the psychological battlefield of identity, linguistic guilt, and sibling rivalry in a gripping one-act monologue where an author confronts her own image on a TV screen!

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: एकालाप / एक ही पात्र द्वारा लंबा भाषण

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Manjula Nayak, a Kannada short-story writer, becomes a sudden international literary celebrity after writing her first English novel. During a TV studio recording, the frozen image of herself on the monitor comes alive and begins interrogating her.

main_concepts.concept_title: 🗣️ The Language Debate: Kannada vs. English
main_concepts.simple_explanation: The play tackles the cultural politics of writing in English versus regional Indian languages. Manjula defends writing in English for global reach, but her image mocks her for betraying her native language for fame and money.
The interrogation uncovers Manjula's deep resentment toward her deceased sister, Malini, who was physically disabled but brilliant, preferred by their parents, and loved by Manjula's own husband.

The climax suggests a shocking revelation: the bestselling English novel was actually written secretly by the bedridden Malini before her death. Manjula merely appropriated and published it as her own, leaving her identity fractured.

fun_activity.title: 🪞 The Mirror Interrogation
fun_activity.instructions: Stand in front of a mirror for 2 minutes. Imagine your reflection is your 'inner critic' who knows all your secrets. What one tough question would your reflection ask you about your biggest ambition?

exam_tips: 📌 Always mention how Girish Karnad uses modern technology (the television monitor) as a dramatic device to represent the protagonist's conscience and subconscious guilt.
📌 Contrast Manjula's public persona (confident, successful, defensive) with her private reality (insecure, jealous, and morally compromised).
📌 Discuss the play's commentary on the Indian literary market—how English-language writers often receive disproportionate wealth and media hype compared to regional writers.
quick_recap: ⭐ The entire one-act play is performed by a single actress playing both Manjula and her electronic Image.
⭐ Karnad masterfully builds suspense through dialogue between a human and a recorded screen.
⭐ The title 'Broken Images' symbolizes Manjula's shattered self-image, broken family bonds, and split linguistic identity.
